about: The bones of the hip and thigh as an anatomy textbook draws them, on both sides: the two hip bones with the joints at the pubis and the sacrum, the sockets of the hip joints, and the thigh bones. Each femur is drawn along the glass thigh to the condyles at the knee end, where the glass leg has almost faded, and the thigh is drawn shorter than a real one because the glass leg is. Select a part, or zoom in on it, to see the finer structures it holds; the Structures list nests them under their parent. The shapes are an adult-mean drawing and not anyone's scan: the iliac wing is a smooth bowed plate, the joint capsule, ligaments, labrum and cartilage are thin schematic shapes, and the bone tissue (compact and spongy bone, an osteon, the canals, the cells and the marrow) is a MAGNIFIED ILLUSTRATION drawn inside the right femur, far larger than life and with counts chosen only to be seen. Bone is not simulated as tissue: calcium handling and bone remodelling are not modelled. The only live part is the red bone marrow of the ilium, which follows erythropoietin.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Hip Bones
parts.summary: The two bones that make the sides of the pelvis
parts.function: Each hip bone is made of three bones, the ilium, the ischium and the pubis, that fuse at the socket of the hip joint. The two hip bones meet in front at the pubic symphysis and join the sacrum behind.

parts.label: Ilium
parts.summary: The broad upper wing of the hip bone
parts.function: The ilium is the largest of the three bones. Its wing carries the weight of the trunk on to the sacrum and gives attachment to the muscles of the buttock and the abdominal wall.

parts.label: Iliac Crest
parts.summary: The curved upper edge of the ilium
parts.function: The iliac crest runs from the front spine of the ilium to the back one, and can be felt through the skin at the waist.

parts.label: Anterior Superior Iliac Spine
parts.summary: The front end of the iliac crest
parts.function: This is the pointed front end of the iliac crest, which can be felt in front of the hip. The inguinal ligament is attached to it.

parts.label: Anterior Inferior Iliac Spine
parts.summary: A lower projection on the front edge of the ilium
parts.function: This spine lies below the anterior superior spine and just above the socket. The straight muscle of the thigh and the iliofemoral ligament are attached to it.

parts.label: Posterior Superior Iliac Spine
parts.summary: The back end of the iliac crest
parts.function: This is the back end of the iliac crest, near the sacrum. Ligaments that bind the ilium to the sacrum are attached near it.

parts.label: Iliac Fossa
parts.summary: The smooth hollow on the inner face of the wing
parts.function: The iliac fossa is the broad, shallow inner surface of the wing, which the iliacus muscle covers. It is drawn as a patch on the wing.

parts.label: Arcuate Line
parts.summary: The ridge along the inner face of the ilium
parts.function: The arcuate line runs round the inner surface of the ilium and forms part of the brim of the true pelvis, the opening that leads from the abdomen into the pelvis.

parts.label: Auricular Surface
parts.summary: The ear-shaped face that meets the sacrum
parts.function: The auricular surface is the rough, ear-shaped area on the back of the inner face of the ilium that forms the sacroiliac joint with the sacrum. It is drawn as a patch.

parts.label: Ischium
parts.summary: The lower and back part of the hip bone
parts.function: The ischium forms the lower part of the socket and the part of the pelvis a person sits on. Its ramus runs forward to meet the pubis.

parts.label: Ischial Tuberosity
parts.summary: The thick rough part a person sits on
parts.function: The ischial tuberosity is the thick, rough lower end of the ischium that bears the weight in sitting. The hamstring muscles are attached to it.

parts.label: Ischial Spine
parts.summary: A pointed projection on the back edge of the ischium
parts.function: The ischial spine projects into the pelvis. It separates the greater sciatic notch above from the lesser sciatic notch below.

parts.label: Ramus of the Ischium
parts.summary: The bar of the ischium that runs forward
parts.function: The ramus of the ischium runs forward and upward from the tuberosity and joins the inferior ramus of the pubis. Together they form one bar along the lower edge of the obturator foramen.

parts.label: Pubis
parts.summary: The front part of the hip bone
parts.function: The pubis forms the front of the pelvis. It has a body and two rami, and the two pubic bones meet at the pubic symphysis.

parts.label: Body of the Pubis
parts.summary: The flat part at the front, beside the midline
parts.function: The body of the pubis is the flattened part next to the midline, which faces its fellow across the pubic symphysis.

parts.label: Superior Pubic Ramus
parts.summary: The upper bar of the pubis
parts.function: The superior ramus runs from the body of the pubis back to the socket and forms the upper edge of the obturator foramen.

parts.label: Inferior Pubic Ramus
parts.summary: The lower bar of the pubis
parts.function: The inferior ramus runs down and back from the body of the pubis and joins the ramus of the ischium, closing the lower edge of the obturator foramen.

parts.label: Pubic Tubercle
parts.summary: A small knob on the upper edge of the pubis
parts.function: The pubic tubercle is a small rounded knob on the front of the superior ramus, near the midline. The inguinal ligament is attached to it.

parts.label: Acetabulum
parts.summary: The cup-shaped socket of the hip joint
parts.function: The acetabulum is the deep cup on the outer face of the hip bone, made by all three bones. It holds the head of the femur. Its lower rim has a gap called the acetabular notch.

parts.label: Obturator Foramen
parts.summary: The large opening between the pubis and the ischium
parts.function: The obturator foramen is the opening framed by the rami of the pubis and the ischium. In life a membrane closes it, with a small gap for the obturator nerve and vessels. It is drawn as a thin pane.

parts.label: Pubic Symphysis
parts.summary: The joint between the two pubic bones
parts.function: At the pubic symphysis the two pubic bones are joined by a pad of fibrocartilage, the interpubic disc. It allows very little movement.

parts.label: Sacroiliac Joints
parts.summary: The joints between the hip bones and the sacrum
parts.function: Each sacroiliac joint joins the auricular surface of the ilium to the sacrum. Strong ligaments hold the joint so that the weight of the trunk passes from the spine to the legs. They are drawn as markers.

parts.label: Greater Sciatic Notches
parts.summary: The large curved gaps on the back edge of the hip bone
parts.function: The greater sciatic notch is the curve in the back edge of the hip bone between the ilium and the ischial spine. In life ligaments close it into a passage for the sciatic nerve and other structures. It is drawn as a line along the edge.

parts.label: Lesser Sciatic Notches
parts.summary: The small gaps on the back edge of the hip bone
parts.function: The lesser sciatic notch is the small curve in the back edge of the ischium, between the ischial spine and the tuberosity. A tendon of the obturator internus passes through it. It is drawn as a line along the edge.

parts.label: Red Bone Marrow (ilium)
parts.summary: Blood-forming marrow in the wing of the hip bone
parts.function: Guyton and Hall list the ilia among the membranous bones that make red blood cells in the adult. Erythropoietin from the kidney drives this production; the text does not say what the other bones hold.

drives.note: Erythropoietin raises red-cell production in red marrow; the cited text names this bone among the sites of adult red-cell production.

parts.label: Femurs
parts.summary: The thigh bones
parts.function: Each femur is the longest and strongest bone of the body. Its rounded head fits the socket of the hip bone, and its lower end, with two condyles, makes part of the knee joint.

parts.label: Head of the Femur
parts.summary: The ball of the hip joint
parts.function: The head of the femur is the smooth, rounded upper end that fits the acetabulum. It is covered with cartilage except at a small pit, the fovea.

parts.label: Fovea of the Head
parts.summary: A small pit in the head
parts.function: The fovea is the small pit in the head of the femur to which the ligament of the head is attached. It is not covered by cartilage.

parts.label: Neck of the Femur
parts.summary: The narrower part between the head and the shaft
parts.function: The neck joins the head to the shaft at an angle, which holds the head in the socket and puts the shaft out to the side. In life this is a common place for the bone to break; here it is drawn at a steeper angle than a real neck because the glass thigh is narrow.

parts.label: Greater Trochanter
parts.summary: The large bump on the outer side of the upper end
parts.function: The greater trochanter is the large bony prominence at the top of the shaft that can be felt at the side of the hip. Most of the muscles of the buttock are attached to it.

parts.label: Lesser Trochanter
parts.summary: The smaller bump on the inner side of the upper end
parts.function: The lesser trochanter is a smaller projection below the neck on the back and inner side. The tendon of the psoas major muscle is attached to it.

parts.label: Intertrochanteric Line
parts.summary: The ridge on the front between the trochanters
parts.function: The intertrochanteric line is a rough ridge on the front of the upper end of the femur. The capsule of the hip joint and the iliofemoral ligament are attached to it.

parts.label: Intertrochanteric Crest
parts.summary: The ridge on the back between the trochanters
parts.function: The intertrochanteric crest is a prominent ridge on the back of the upper end of the femur, running between the two trochanters.

parts.label: Linea Aspera
parts.summary: The rough ridge down the back of the shaft
parts.function: The linea aspera is the rough ridge that runs down the back of the shaft. Many of the muscles of the thigh are attached to it.

parts.label: Shaft of the Femur
parts.summary: The long body of the bone
parts.function: The shaft is the long, nearly cylindrical middle of the femur, slightly bowed forward. It is drawn to the knee end where the glass thigh fades.

parts.label: Hip Joints
parts.summary: The ball-and-socket joints of the hips
parts.function: Each hip joint is the head of the femur in the acetabulum. It is strong and stable and still allows movement in every direction. It is drawn as a disc across the opening of the socket.

parts.label: Acetabular Labrum
parts.summary: A rim of fibrocartilage round the socket
parts.function: The acetabular labrum is a ring of fibrocartilage attached to the edge of the acetabulum that deepens the socket. It is drawn as a ring.

parts.label: Ligament of the Head of the Femur
parts.summary: A small ligament from the notch to the head
parts.function: This ligament runs from the acetabular notch to the fovea of the head of the femur. It is drawn as a short cord.

parts.label: Joint Capsule (hip)
parts.summary: The strong fibrous sleeve round the joint
parts.function: The capsule of the hip joint runs from the rim of the acetabulum to the neck of the femur and encloses the joint. It is strengthened by three ligaments. It is drawn as a faint glass sleeve.

parts.label: Iliofemoral Ligament
parts.summary: The strong Y-shaped ligament in front of the joint
parts.function: The iliofemoral ligament runs from the anterior inferior iliac spine to the intertrochanteric line, and stops the hip from being bent back too far.

parts.label: Pubofemoral Ligament
parts.summary: The ligament in front and below the joint
parts.function: The pubofemoral ligament runs from the pubic bone to the lower part of the capsule. It limits how far the thigh can be moved out to the side.

parts.label: Ischiofemoral Ligament
parts.summary: The ligament behind the joint
parts.function: The ischiofemoral ligament runs from the ischium to the neck of the femur behind the joint, and limits inward rotation.

parts.label: Synovial Membrane (hip)
parts.summary: The lining of the joint capsule
parts.function: The synovial membrane lines the capsule and covers the parts of the neck inside the joint. It makes the synovial fluid that lubricates the joint. It is drawn as a faint glass sleeve inside the capsule.

parts.label: Articular Cartilage (socket)
parts.summary: The cartilage that lines the socket
parts.function: The lunate surface of the acetabulum is covered with articular cartilage, so that the head of the femur glides on it with little friction. The cartilage on the head itself is drawn with the femur.

parts.label: Compact Bone
parts.summary: The dense outer layer of the shaft
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Compact bone is the dense, hard outer layer of a long bone. It is built of osteons, with layers of lamellae round them and between them.

parts.label: Osteon (Haversian system)
parts.summary: The working unit of compact bone
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. An osteon is a cylinder of concentric bone layers around a central canal that carries a blood vessel and a nerve. Osteons run along the length of the shaft. It is drawn far larger than real.

parts.label: Central (Haversian) Canal
parts.summary: The channel down the middle of an osteon
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. The central canal carries the blood vessels and nerves that supply the osteon.

parts.label: Concentric Lamellae
parts.summary: The layers of bone round the canal
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. The lamellae are thin layers of bone matrix wrapped round the central canal like the rings of a tree. They are drawn as three glass cylinders, and the number of layers is chosen to be seen.

parts.label: Lacunae and Osteocytes
parts.summary: Small spaces in the lamellae that hold bone cells
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. A lacuna is a small space in the bone matrix that holds one osteocyte, a mature bone cell. They lie between and within the lamellae. The number drawn is chosen to be seen.

parts.label: Canaliculi
parts.summary: Tiny channels that join the lacunae
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Canaliculi are very fine channels that join the lacunae to each other and to the central canal, so that the cells can pass nutrients and signals along them.

parts.label: Perforating (Volkmann) Canals
parts.summary: Channels across the bone that join the vessels
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Perforating canals run across the bone at an angle to the osteons and join the vessels of the central canals to those of the periosteum and the marrow cavity.

parts.label: Periosteum
parts.summary: The tough membrane on the outside of the bone
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. The periosteum is the fibrous membrane that covers the outer surface of the bone except at the joint surfaces. It carries blood vessels and nerves and has a layer of cells that can form new bone. It is drawn as a faint glass sleeve.

parts.label: Endosteum
parts.summary: The thin lining of the marrow cavity
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. The endosteum is a thin layer of cells that lines the inner surface of compact bone, next to the marrow cavity. It is drawn as a faint glass sleeve.

parts.label: Circumferential Lamellae
parts.summary: Layers that run right round the shaft
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Circumferential lamellae are layers of bone that run all the way round the shaft, just under the periosteum on the outside and next to the endosteum on the inside. They are drawn as thin glass cylinders.

parts.label: Interstitial Lamellae
parts.summary: Fragments of old layers between the osteons
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Interstitial lamellae are the remains of older osteons that have been partly replaced as the bone is renewed, left between the newer ones. They are drawn as short arcs.

parts.label: Spongy (Cancellous) Bone
parts.summary: The lattice inside the ends of the bone
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Spongy bone is a lattice of thin plates and rods with spaces between, found in the ends of long bones such as the head, neck and trochanter of the femur and its condyles. It is drawn as glass blobs holding the lattice.

parts.label: Trabeculae
parts.summary: The rods and plates of the lattice
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Trabeculae are the thin bars of bone that make up spongy bone. They lie along the lines of stress in the bone. The number and pattern drawn are chosen to be seen.

parts.label: Red Marrow Spaces
parts.summary: The spaces between the trabeculae
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. The spaces between the trabeculae are filled with marrow. In the places the cited text names, this marrow makes red blood cells; the text does not say that the femur's own is red, so these are drawn as a generic marrow space.

parts.label: Medullary Cavity
parts.summary: The hollow in the middle of the shaft
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. The medullary cavity is the central space of the shaft of a long bone, lined by the endosteum and filled with marrow. It makes the bone light for its strength. It is drawn as a faint glass cylinder.

parts.label: Yellow Marrow
parts.summary: Fatty marrow in the cavity of the shaft
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. In the adult the marrow of the shaft of most long bones has turned to fat and is called yellow marrow. Guyton and Hall note that this change happens in most long bones after about the age of twenty.

parts.label: Bone Cells
parts.summary: The three kinds of cell that build and remodel bone
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Bone is alive: osteoblasts build new bone, osteocytes maintain it, and osteoclasts remove it. They are drawn far larger than life, at one example site each. Their activity is not simulated.

parts.label: Osteoblasts
parts.summary: Cells that build new bone
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Osteoblasts are the cells that make new bone matrix. They line the surface of bone that is being laid down, here a row on the lining of the marrow cavity.

parts.label: Osteocytes
parts.summary: Mature bone cells held in the matrix
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Osteocytes are mature bone cells that have become surrounded by matrix, each in its own lacuna. They reach one another by long fine processes that run through the canaliculi.

parts.label: Osteoclasts
parts.summary: Large cells that remove bone
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. Osteoclasts are large cells with several nuclei that break down bone matrix. They sit in shallow pits on the surface they are eroding. Together with the osteoblasts they let the bone be renewed.

parts.label: Epiphyseal Line
parts.summary: The scar where the bone once grew in length
parts.function: Magnified illustration inside the right femur. In a growing person the end of a long bone is separated from the shaft by a plate of cartilage where the bone grows in length. When growth stops the plate turns to bone and leaves the epiphyseal line. It is drawn as a ring at each end.

parts.label: Articular Cartilage (femur)
parts.summary: The cartilage on the joint surfaces of the femur
parts.function: Articular cartilage covers the head of the femur and the two condyles, so that the joint surfaces glide with little friction. It is drawn as thin caps.
